column1: # The Objective-C type encodings the game's tables keep as literals (bead oo-dbz.3, ADR-0056 amendment
# oo-dbz.3). Measured with clang's @encode() on main eae8c876d (the last tree built as Objective-C++,
# with libobjc2), by the probe `python3 tools/gen-type-encodings.py --probe <file.mm>` writes, compiled
# with oolite.exe's Objective-C++ flags and run; --compare <its output> checks this file against a
# measurement. tools/gen-type-encodings.py renders oolite-dev/src/Core/OOTypeEncodings.h from it.
# key<TAB>measured spellings<TAB>encoding. The key is the C++ type kOOTypeEncoding<> is specialised
# for; the measured spellings are the names the tables and tests write, every one measured, which
# name the key's type (typedefs of it) and so share its encoding. id and SEL, which C++ has not, are
# keyed by the tag types OOObjCId and OOObjCSelector.
